subtopic: Share Class Eligibility and Account Types
source_evidence: Retirement share classes are typically only available through an employer-sponsored retirement plan, such as a 401(k).
answer: Mutual fund share classes can have different account and eligibility requirements. For example, retirement share classes are typically available only through an employer-sponsored plan such as a 401(k). Retail no-load shares are commonly available through a brokerage account, a fund family, or an investment advisory account. Some Institutional (Class I) shares may also be available to retail investors through an employer plan or advisory account, even when investing directly would require a high minimum. So, when comparing classes, consider how you plan to invest—directly, through an adviser, or through an employer plan—and check which classes are available through that account.
